name: Insulin lispro
route_note: subcutaneous injection within 15 minutes of a meal or via insulin pump; IV under supervision

discovery.note: Reversing proline B28 and lysine B29 (the sequence found in IGF-1) weakens hexamer formation so the analogue is absorbed quickly.

tagline: The first rapid-acting insulin analogue, built by swapping two amino acids
summary: Insulin lispro is a rapid-acting insulin analogue taken at mealtimes or used in insulin pumps. Approved as Humalog in 1996, it was the first insulin analogue on the market; its onset of about 15 minutes better matches the rise in blood glucose after meals than regular human insulin.
mechanism: Lispro has the B28 proline and B29 lysine of human insulin reversed. This reduces self-association into dimers and hexamers, so after subcutaneous injection it dissociates and is absorbed rapidly, with onset in about 15 minutes, peak at 30–90 minutes and duration of 3–5 hours.
Once absorbed it acts on the insulin receptor exactly like human insulin, promoting glucose uptake and storage and inhibiting hepatic glucose output, lipolysis and ketogenesis.
uses: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (prandial insulin and pump therapy)
Type 2 diabetes mellitus requiring mealtime insulin

history.title: Humalog approved
history.detail: FDA approves Humalog in June 1996, the first commercially available insulin analogue; it is also approved in the EU in 1996.

history.title: Premixed formulation
history.detail: Humalog Mix75/25, a mix of lispro with lispro protamine suspension, is approved in the US.

history.title: Follow-on product
history.detail: FDA approves Sanofi's Admelog, a follow-on insulin lispro.

history.title: Lower-priced unbranded version
history.detail: Lilly launches an unbranded Insulin Lispro at half the Humalog list price in the US.

history.title: Ultra-rapid Lyumjev
history.detail: Lyumjev, lispro with treprostinil and citrate to speed absorption, is approved in the EU, Japan and US.

pk.half_life: about 1 h after SC dose; action lasts 3–5 h
pk.metabolism: proteolytic degradation as for human insulin

facts: Humalog was the first recombinant insulin analogue to reach the market (1996).
The B28/B29 sequence inversion in lispro mirrors the corresponding sequence of insulin-like growth factor 1.
